newsitem.title: UK: IBCA upgrades Finland foreign currency rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA upgrades Finland foreign currency rating.

text.p: The Republic of Finland, bolstered by economic and fiscal improvements, received a credit upgrade on Tuesday from European rating agency IBCA.
Finland's long-term foreign currency rating was raised to AA plus from AA, while its local currency ratings were affirmed, IBCA said.

"Finland's impressive resilience in the face of sharper economic shocks in the last recession than those faced by any other Western European country have demonstrated once again the country's remarkable social cohesion," IBCA said in a statement.

The agency said Finland's political leadership over EMU, as well as the fact that the country already satisfies the Maastricht criteria, strengthened the belief that Finland would be among the first wave of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) members.
Among the many benefits of EMU, it will lock in the lower real interest rates that have already been achieved, IBCA said.
It said these factors acted to offset the country's one enduring weakness, its continued over-dependence on forestry.

"Even here progress has been made in moving upmarket from bulk pulp to higher quality paper and other products, as well as in developing electronics, services and other non-forest sectors," IBCA said.
As reasons for the upgrade, the agency cited the steady and significant progress made in most aspects of the economy.

"Finland's public finances are now sound. The public debt ratio has stabilised at a level below the Maastricht criterion. A further plus point is that fiscal adjustment has been achieved almost wholly on the expenditure side, with no significant tax increases," said IBCA.
It added that net external debt had fallen sharply and was expected to do so again this year, in which case there would be no net foreign borrowing by the state at all.

"The buoyancy of the export sector and continued industrial diversification, especially in electronics where Nokia has become a world standard setter, have produced consistent current account surpluses - the source of the steady external debt reduction - and consistent real economic growth," IBCA said.

The agency said firm monetary policy, together with limited growth in wages negotiated by unions, employers and government in a tripartite structure, has ensured economic growth had been accompanied by stable prices.
IBCA said Finland had one of the lowest rates of inflation in Europe.
"The weak point has been unemployment. It has fallen consistently since 1994 but at a disappointingly slow rate as rapid productivity growth has dampened the demand for labour," IBCA said.
